title: Two-step behavior on an aligned pair
statement: Let $first,second$ be Boolean flags, and let Boolean words $x,pre,rest,a$ and bits $b,c$ satisfy $x=pre\mathbin{++}[b,c]\mathbin{++}rest$. Starting from the pair extractor's block-start configuration at input position $|pre|$, with buffer $a$, work-head position $|a|$, and empty output, after two steps the configuration is as follows: if $b=c$, it remains in the block-start state at position $|pre|+2$, with buffer $a\mathbin{++}[b]$, head at the end of that buffer, and empty output; if $b=1,c=0$, it is halted at position $|pre|+2$, with buffer $a$, head at $|a|$, and empty output; if $b=0,c=1$, it is in the rewind state at position $|pre|+2$, with buffer $a$, head one cell before its end, and empty output.
hypotheses_covered: first and second are Boolean flags
x, pre, rest, and a are Boolean words
x=pre followed by b, c, and rest
replaced:
If the input splits as $x = p\, b\, c\, r$ with bits $b, c$, then two
extractor steps from the block-start state at position $\abs{p}$ with buffer
$a$ append $b$ to the buffer and continue when $b = c$; halt silently when
$(b,c) = (1,0)$; and enter the rewind phase with the work head one cell before
the end of the buffer when $(b,c) = (0,1)$. In all three cases nothing is
emitted.
